questions.q: '___ honesty is the best policy.' Which article, and why?
questions.a: Zero — abstract uncountable used generically. A wrong answer 'the honesty' reveals the student marks every noun as needing an article — the over-specification error, from Hindi where abstract nouns can take determiners differently.

'a European' (yoo- consonant sound) and 'an honest man' (silent h → vowel sound). A wrong answer 'an European' proves the student applies the rule to spelling, not pronunciation — the single most-tested determiner trap.

questions.q: 'She goes to ___ school by bus' vs 'The parents met at ___ school.'
questions.a: First: zero article (school-as-purpose: to study). Second: 'the school' (the building, a place). A wrong answer putting 'the' in the first reveals the student doesn't know institutions drop 'the' when used for their purpose — go to school/hospital/church/bed.

questions.q: Article choice follows a ______ algorithm: (1) Is the noun specific/known to both speaker and listener?
Fill in the blank: Article choice follows a two-question ______: (1) Is the noun specific/known to both speaker and listener? → 'the'.
Fill in the blank: The dog was huge.' First ______ = 'a' (new information), second = 'the' (now we both know which dog).
What is Article choice follows a two-question algorithm? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Article choice follows a two-question algorithm: (1) Is the noun specific/known to both speaker and listener? → 'the'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Article choice follows a two-question algorithm: (______) Is the noun specific/known to both speaker and listener? → 'the'.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Article choice follows a two-question algorithm?
questions.a: Students choose 'an' by spelling (writing 'an university'), use 'the' for general categories ('the dogs are faithful animals' — generic plural takes zero), and omit 'the' before unique objects.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student runs the specificity algorithm on any noun phrase — including uncountables, plurals, and proper nouns — and explains each choice by shared-knowledge vs first-mention, plus the vowel-sound rule for an (an hour, a university).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The dog was huge.' First mention = 'a' (new ______), second = 'the' (now we both know which dog).
